And in the year 594 [died] {OCR?} Aqsunqur, lord of Sinjar and of Nisibis and of the Khabur and of Callinicus (Raqqa);
and in his place reigned his son, Qutb al-Din Muhammad;
and Shuja' al-Din bar Yaqash, his father's servant, became his administrator.
And in the same year, the prince Nur al-Din Arslan Shah, lord of Mosul, marched against Nisibis,
and took it from Qutb al-Din Muhammad, his cousin;
for the reason that Qutb al-Din had laid his hand upon certain villages of the region of Mesopotamia within the border of Mosul.
And when he sent an envoy demanding that he return them, but he was not willing,
Nur al-Din gathered an army and marched against Nisibis.
And Qutb al-Din also came,
and he was routed and fled to Harran.
And he sent to al-Adil
and asked help from him.
When Nur al-Din entered Nisibis,
and stayed in it for some days,
sickness broke out among his troops,
and six of the famous nobles of Mosul died,
among whom was Mujahid al-Din Qaymaz, his administrator.
And for this reason (and therefore), Nur al-Din abandoned Nisibis and came to Mosul,
and Qutb al-Din, its lord, took possession of it again.
And in the same year the Khwarazmshah marched against the city of Bukhara,
and took it from the people of Khata, that is to say, the Chinese.
And because the Muslim Bukharans were very content with the Chinese,
in that although they were without religion (infidels),
they were nevertheless very wise and just,
they fought very fiercely on the walls.
So much so that
they took a dog, dressed it in garments like the Khwarazmshah's, threw it towards the Khwarazmians, and said,
"This is your king."
Now the Khwarazmshah, when he took the city by the sword,
did not remember against them their foolishness,
but even gave them gold,
and made them swear fealty before him.
And in the same year King al-Adil came and encamped against Mardin,
and fought against it fiercely.
And its lord was a young boy, Husam al-Din,
and his administrator was Nizam al-Din bar Yaqash.
And when the inhabitants of the city acted treacherously,
they surrendered the city to al-Adil.
And his forces entered and plundered it,
and committed outrages in it.
